candidates.title: The Shawl He Already Brought
candidates.one_line_concept: Zuv notices Aachu will get cold before she admits it, and the folded shawl becomes proof of being quietly known.
suggested_slide_arc: Aachu steps out confidently without a layer while Zuv notices the evening breeze.
Zuv carries the shawl folded over his arm without making a fuss.
Aachu gets cold on a bench or terrace, trying to hide it.
Zuv drapes the shawl over both of them, turning care into closeness.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Aachu at a doorway in light evening wind, Zuv just behind her holding a folded shawl low at his side.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: Both seated close under the same shawl, couple lower-frame, upper-middle left open for handwritten text.
candidates.visual_potential: Large recurring prop, romantic fabric movement, simple locations, strong proof of attention, premium watercolor softness.

candidates.title: The Hair Tie He Kept
candidates.one_line_concept: Zuv starts carrying Aachu's hair tie because he noticed she always needs one at the exact wrong time.
suggested_slide_arc: Aachu searches her wrist or bag as wind lifts her hair.
Zuv quietly reveals the hair tie on his wrist or keyring.
Aachu laughs at how naturally he planned for her.
The hair tie sits between their hands like a tiny love language.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Aachu holding her hair back in a breezy cafe corner while Zuv watches with an almost-hidden smile.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: Close but not crowded view of Zuv offering the hair tie in his open palm, Aachu smiling beside him.
candidates.visual_potential: Fresh intimate prop, very shareable micro-observation, strong hand/face staging if kept simple.

candidates.title: The Tea That Waited For Me
candidates.one_line_concept: Aachu comes back late to find Zuv has kept her tea warm in the exact way she likes.
suggested_slide_arc: A quiet table with one untouched cup and soft steam.
Zuv reheats or protects the cup with both hands.
Aachu returns tired, noticing the small setup before noticing him.
They sit together over the warm cup, the care finally visible.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: A warm ivory table scene with one cup, coaster, spoon, and Zuv partly visible waiting nearby.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: Aachu seated with the cup while Zuv sits close, their hands near the saucer but not tangled.
candidates.visual_potential: Extremely feasible, cozy, prop-led, with generous negative space and low anatomy risk.

candidates.title: The Umbrella That Made Us Walk Slower
candidates.one_line_concept: Rain turns a normal walk into an excuse for Aachu and Zuv to move closer than necessary.
suggested_slide_arc: First raindrops appear while they stand near a doorway or street edge.
One umbrella opens between them, slightly too small.
They walk slower through soft puddle reflections.
They reach shelter but keep standing close under the umbrella.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Zuv opening one umbrella as Aachu looks up at the rain, with a clean pale background.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: The couple under one umbrella at the edge of shelter, shoes near puddles, upper area clear for text.
candidates.visual_potential: Strong romantic silhouette, beautiful watercolor rain, clear slide progression, but must avoid generic rainy-couple staging.

candidates.title: The Last Bite Treaty
candidates.one_line_concept: Zuv keeps pretending he does not want the last bite because he already knows Aachu does.
suggested_slide_arc: A small dessert plate sits between them with one bite left.
Aachu says no with her hands, while still looking at the plate.
Zuv quietly slides the plate toward her.
Aachu takes the bite as Zuv smiles like this was always the plan.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: A shared table scene with one plate, two forks, and the final bite clearly visible.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: The plate gently pushed toward Aachu, Zuv's hand retreating, both faces calm and fond.
candidates.visual_potential: Simple, readable, charming, and low-risk; best as a compact 3-4 slide carousel so the payoff does not thin out.

top_pick.title: The Shawl He Already Brought
top_pick.rationale: It has the strongest mix of visual proof, romance, prop clarity, and imagegen safety. The shawl is large enough to read instantly, supports consistent wardrobe and body language, and gives a natural emotional payoff without needing crowded scenes or tiny details.

visual_risks.risk: Wrapping, tying, or close hand interactions can create awkward fingers or impossible arm positions.
visual_risks.prevention: Prefer offering, holding, draping, or shared-cover poses over complex tying actions.

visual_risks.risk: Busy rain, cafe tables, or fabric folds can compete with handwritten text.
visual_risks.prevention: Keep text in upper-middle negative space with the couple and props lower-frame.

visual_risks.risk: Rain, tea, and last-bite moments can become familiar romance tropes if not anchored in a specific Aachu/Zuv habit.
visual_risks.prevention: Make the proof object specific and recurring: shawl, hair tie, exact cup ritual, single plate gesture.

visual_risks.risk: Too many props or micro-actions in one slide can reduce face consistency and scene clarity.
visual_risks.prevention: Use one hero prop per idea and one readable action per slide.

The Shawl He Already Brought.note: Four slides gives setup, noticed care, need, and payoff. Five only if adding a strong breeze/terrace transition.

The Hair Tie He Kept.note: Needs enough beats for the tiny prop to become emotionally clear; avoid six because the object is small.

The Tea That Waited For Me.note: Best as a compact ritual; too many slides may feel repetitive.

The Umbrella That Made Us Walk Slower.note: Rain gives scene variety, but more than five risks generic scenic padding.

The Last Bite Treaty.note: The payoff is sweet but small; keep it tight.
